wave_title: Continuing the W3 donor-research pivot from the prior generation (souffle), censused buck2's own incremental-computation engine, Dice. Unlike every other W3 donor censused so far (which each model exactly ONE evolving computation state), Dice's own stated driving design goal is 'multiple concurrently evolving lineages of state' -- a tree of branches, not a single revision line -- directly matching Atlas's own MULTI-AI-CONSTRUCTION-FABRIC.md language ('concurrent speculative CandidateAtlas branches with separate CandidateChangeSet/evidence lineage'), making this plausibly the single most directly relevant piece of real, working prior art for that specific future Atlas-native capability found in the W3 lane so far.
priority_classification: semantic preservation / roadmap advancement (R5's own donor lane, and directly informative for the later AIF1/Multi-AI-Construction-Fabric target architecture) -- real donor research, continuing the pivot away from the code-correctness vein this session mined extensively (18 generations) once it stopped yielding well-evidenced candidates.
method: Read `dice/docs/incrementality.md` -- the donor's OWN primary design document, not merely its code -- Introduction/§1, Soundness/§3.3-3.4, Branches/§4.2, Injected keys/§4.3, Resolution/§4.4, and the fork operation/§5.4 (including the document's own stated Lemma and topological-sort algorithm sketch for fork-time reverse-dependency-map reconciliation). Cross-checked the document's own data-structure description against the real `dice_core/src/branch.rs` struct definition and `dice_core/src/lib.rs`'s module doc comment to confirm the design document matches the actual shipped implementation, not merely aspirational design prose. Also read `dice/dice/src/lib.rs`'s top-level crate doc comment and worked example to confirm the injected-vs-computed key distinction is a real public API, not only an internal core-state concept.
key_finding: Dice models state as a TREE of branches (not a single revision line), where forking is cheap because resolution transparently, lazily delegates to the parent branch at the exact fork-point version when the current branch has no claim of its own for a key -- avoiding any upfront state copy. The real cost of this cheap-forking design is a nontrivial, invariant-preserving reconciliation of the new branch's own reverse-dependency map at fork time (a topological attached/residual partition over candidate keys drawn only from the parent's own rdep map, never a full state scan), which the donor's own design document treats as 'the crux of this algorithm.' The document additionally states and proves an explicit soundness theorem: `lookup` returning `Unknown` is always sound by design, mirroring Atlas's own `EpistemicStatus`/evidence discipline as a PROVEN property of a real, production-scale (Meta's own build system) incremental-computation engine, not merely an Atlas-internal convention.
